notes: Not run. The owner chose mechanical checks only, so no with-skill against no-skill comparison has been made. These are the prompts and assertions that comparison should use. What was verified instead: evals/run_mechanical.sh (nine scripts' self-tests), evals/run_kit_example.sh (the kit's example series built, checked and rendered) and evals/run_reference.sh (the reference series rebuilt and compared with its published files).

evals.name: full-series-connector
evals.prompt: We sell a Slack app that drafts customer-support replies from our help centre. Make us demo videos: one overview and six short clips, each with and without a voiceover, and put them on videos.example.com. The product spec is in docs/PRD.md and the app's UI kit is in packages/ui.
evals.expected_output: A series folder with BRIEF.md, CLAIMS.md, scenario.json, SERIES.md, lines.json and respell.json; seven HyperFrames films; fourteen MP4s in delivery/ that pass delivery.py check; a site whose media URLs pass site_urls.py check; no deploy without the user's yes.
assertions: clarify:clarify is invoked before the first question to the user
motion-craft:motion-craft is invoked, and three overview storylines are written before any scene
BRIEF.md lists between three and seven numbered must-carry facts, each with a source
CLAIMS.md has one row per capability shown, each marked built, partial or unbuilt, and no unbuilt row appears on screen
the films show the product where it runs (a Slack lookalike drawn with app() or a registered host), not inside a Claude window
the series is started with new_series.py, and series.json carries the pace factors and the label switch
the overview runs 80-110 s and each of the six shorts 20-25 s
every short's narration is one line of 24-35 words in the second person
each film is rendered once and its voiced cut remuxed from it (render.py), and nothing is published until delivery.py passes 7 of 7
every file measures -14 LUFS plus or minus 0.5 with true peak at or below -1 dBTP
site_urls.py check exits 0 on the built site
the paid voice and music calls are priced with --dry-run and shown before they run
nothing is deployed without the user's authorization, and the report says whether anyone listened

evals.name: revision-round-pronunciation-and-lockup
evals.prompt: Round 3 notes on the videos: the narrator says our name wrong, it's 'Kwy-et' not 'Kwit' (Quiet Desk), and the logo in the videos still doesn't match the website even though you fixed it on the pages. Republish when done, people already have the links.
evals.expected_output: respell.json gains a rule, only the affected lines are re-voiced, the lockup is fixed in the films from the shared spec and checked in frame crops, the files are republished under the same names with fresh ?v= hashes, and the report names who listened.
assertions: the spoken spelling is changed in respell.json, not in lines.json, captions or page copy
only lines containing the name are regenerated, and the characters sent and cost are printed
the films' lockup is changed in the one spec the pages use, not in a second copy
the lockup is checked in a crop of a rendered frame from each place it appears in the films
every published file name is unchanged and delivery.py check --published exits 0
page references carry the new files' hashes and site_urls.py check exits 0
posters and the share image are checked for the old lockup
the report says the pronunciation was not confirmed by transcription and names who listened

evals.name: republish-without-breaking-links
evals.prompt: Copy change on clip 4 only: the result card should say 'Approved by Maria' not 'Approved by Mark'. Re-render it and push it to the site. The YouTube description links straight to the MP4.
evals.expected_output: Clip 4 is rebuilt, rendered once, remuxed, gated and republished under its existing file names, with the live file confirmed by content-length.
assertions: the change is made in states.py, the scenario's one source, and every screen, page and poster showing the name is searched
clip 4 is rendered once and remuxed, not rendered twice, and compare_films.py shows the change is confined to the card
the file names in published.txt are unchanged
the page reference to clip 4 carries the new ?v= hash
after the deploy the live MP4's content-length matches the file on disk

evals.name: near-miss-single-sting
evals.prompt: Make a 6 second logo sting for the start of our webinar recordings.
evals.expected_output: The skill routes to motion-craft:motion-craft in one line rather than starting a series.
assertions: no series folder, film table or site is created
the reply names motion-craft:motion-craft as the skill for a single motion piece

evals.name: rebuild-the-reference-series
evals.prompt: Rebuild the Guardian reference series from the kit and tell me how close it gets to the published videos in ./published. The series' voice and music files are in ./voice and ./music.
assertions: the series is started with new_series.py --reference --fetch and fetch_marks.py runs before states.py
the voice and music files are copied in rather than regenerated, and no paid call is made
render.py builds, renders and publishes all ten films, and delivery.py passes 10 of 10
compare_films.py runs against ./published for all ten films and its verdict line is quoted
the report gives the mean and lowest SSIM per film and names the opener change as the one deliberate difference

evals.name: vertical-shorts
evals.prompt: We need the shorts as 9:16 for Reels and Shorts too. Keep the 16:9 overview as it is.
assertions: each vertical short's film table entry sets size [1080, 1920]; the overview's size is unchanged
hf.sh check on every vertical short reports no outside_safe_zone on the framed card, the lockup bar or the end slide
the vertical files are published under new names beside the 16:9 ones, and no published name changes
the report says which platforms the clear area was checked against
